Raised in Liverpool as the half-nephew of a Nazi dictator, this man later fought against his own uncle's regime in the US Navy — who is he, after changing his name postwar?
William Stuart-Houston: Half-nephew of Adolf Hitler (1911–1987)
October 1973: the holiest day of the Jewish calendar collided with the 10th day of Ramadan when Arab forces launched a surprise attack on Israel. What war broke out?
Yom Kippur War: 1973 war between Israel and Arab states.
Which of these people was born first?
Zhuge Liang (born 181) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
John Ray (born 1627) is the earliest of the four. John Ray (29 November 1627 – 17 January 1705) was an English Christian naturalist and one of the earliest English parson-naturalists.

Messerschmitt Bf 109 (founded 1937) is the earliest of the four. The Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW).
Which of these four is the oldest release?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Edwin McMillan is a physicist. McMillan co-invented the synchrotron with Vladimir Veksler, and after the war he returned to the Berkeley Radiation Laboratory to build them.
Pick the chemist from these four.
Maud Menten is a chemist. Maud Leonora Menten (March 20, 1879 – July 17, 1960) was a Canadian physician and chemist.
What is the atomic number of Silicon?
Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
In what year was Max Born?
Max Born: During World War I, Born was originally placed as a radio operator, but his specialist knowledge led to his being moved to research duties on sound ranging.
In what year was Fermat's Last Theorem discovered?
Fermat's Last Theorem: The proposition was first stated as a theorem by Pierre de Fermat around 1637 in the margin of a copy of Arithmetica.
In what year was Selenium discovered?
Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
Metoprolol: Pfizer. It is also used to prevent further heart problems after myocardial infarction and to prevent headaches in those with migraines.
Publishing: Germany. It has various divisions such as trade/retail publishing of fiction and non-fiction, educational publishing, and academic and scientific publishing.
Who is credited with discovering Malaria?
Malaria: Ronald Ross. Malaria is a mosquito-borne infectious disease that is transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes.
Who is credited with discovering Kwashiorkor?
Kwashiorkor: Cicely Williams. Kwashiorkor ( KWOSH-ee-OR-kor, -⁠kər) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.
Who is credited with discovering Titanium?
Titanium: William Gregor. Titanium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ti and atomic number 22.
When a message is designed to spark an immediate purchase, it's called the 'direct-response' kind of this consumer-facing practice. What is it?
Advertising is the practice and techniques employed to bring attention to a product or service.
Named after a French physicist considered a father of electromagnetism, this SI unit measures electric current as one coulomb of charge passing a point per second. What unit is it?
Ampere (symbol: A), often shortened to amp, is the unit of electric current in the International System of Units (SI).
More than 500 orb-weaving spider species, including the familiar garden spider, belong to this genus first classified in 1757 — which genus?
Araneus is a genus of common orb-weaving spiders with more than 500 species, among which are the European garden spider and the barn spider.

These shelled marine crustaceans, cousins to crabs and lobsters, spend their adult lives cemented in place filtering food from the water — and folklore once claimed geese hatched fully formed from one variety. What are they?
Barnacle are arthropods of the subclass Cirripedia in the subphylum Crustacea.

Thought to be the world's most abundant bird of prey in its family, with an estimated 6.7 million individuals, this opportunistic raptor is known for its angled wings and distinctive forked tail — what is it?
Black kite (Milvus migrans) is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors.

This shield-shaped insect, native to East Asia, was accidentally introduced to Allentown, Pennsylvania in 1998 and became a major agricultural pest feeding on over 100 plant species — what insect is it?
Brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.

Once thought to not really exist as a stable molecule, this compound was confirmed since around 1990 to have a real, if fleeting, existence — lasting only about 20 milliseconds at body temperature — what compound is it?
Carbonic acid is a chemical compound with the chemical formula H2CO3.
Atomic number 17, this strongly oxidising yellow-green gas sits between fluorine and bromine on the periodic table — what element is it?
Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.
What's the scientific family name for the group of birds that includes both doves and pigeons — stout-bodied birds with small heads and no formal distinction between the two common names?
Columbidae is a bird family consisting of doves and pigeons.
Bottle gourds, bitter melon, and the fibrous fruit that gives us loofah sponges are all members of which roughly 965-species plant family?
Cucurbitaceae (kew-), also called cucurbits or the gourd family, are a plant family consisting of about 965 species in 101 genera.
First discovered in 1877 and named the following year for its unique double-beamed tail bones, this genus of long-necked sauropod dinosaur roamed Late Jurassic North America — what is it?
Diplodocus (or) is an extinct genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs known from the Late Jurassic of North America.
This mammal family includes living species from two genera as well as extinct giants like the woolly mammoth, and was first scientifically described in 1821 — what family is it?

Elephantidae is a family of large, herbivorous proboscidean mammals which includes the living elephants (belonging to the genera Elephas and Loxodonta), as well as a number of extinct genera like Mammuthus (mammoths) and Palaeoloxodon.

The telltale earth mounds this tunneling mammal pushes to the surface come from its constantly expanding burrow system, and it feeds mainly on earthworms paralyzed by toxins in its saliva — what animal is it?
European mole (Talpa europaea) is a mammal of the order Eulipotyphla.
This American physician-scientist discovered genes tied to several diseases, led the Human Genome Project, and went on to direct the NIH under three presidents — who is he?
Francis Collins (born April 14, 1950) is an American physician-scientist who discovered the genes associated with a number of diseases and led the Human Genome Project.

A 1946 civilian demonstrator version of this British fighter became the world's first civilian-registered jet aircraft, decades after it debuted as the Allies' sole combat jet of World War II — which aircraft?
Gloster Meteor was the first British jet fighter and the Allies' only jet aircraft to engage in combat operations during the Second World War.

This herbivorous mammal, the largest in its family of lagomorphs, nests in shallow ground depressions called 'forms' and is built for speed with long hind legs and heat-dissipating ears — what animal is it?
Hare are mammals belonging to the genus Lepus.
This American physicist threw out the wave-function collapse postulate, instead folding the observer into the same quantum state — an idea later known as the many-worlds interpretation. Who was he?
Hugh Everett III (November 11, 1930 - July 19, 1982) was an American physicist who proposed the relative state interpretation of quantum mechanics.

According to Alfred Adler, this persistent psychological feeling of being deficient compared to others — often rooted in childhood upbringing or social status — can drive a person to overcompensate. Name the concept?
Inferiority complex is a consistent feeling of inadequacy, often resulting in the belief that one is in some way deficient, or inferior, to others.
A former Chicago financial options trader, this internet entrepreneur co-founded a nonprofit free encyclopedia as well as the for-profit wiki host Fandom — who is he?
Jimmy Wales (born August 8, 1966) is an American and British internet entrepreneur and former financial trader.

Normally part of the healthy flora in the mouth, skin, and gut, this rod-shaped bacterium can turn destructive if aspirated into the lungs, producing a telltale bloody, brick-colored jelly-like sputum — what's the organism?
Klebsiella pneumoniae is a Gram-negative, non-motile, encapsulated, lactose-fermenting, facultative anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium.

Equal to about 9.46 trillion kilometres, this astronomical distance unit is defined by how far illumination travels through a vacuum in 365.25 days — despite its name, it isn't a measure of time. What is it?
Light-year (ly or lyr), is a unit of length used to express astronomical distances and is equal to exactly 9460730472580.8 km, which is approximately 9.46 trillion kilometres or 5.88 trillion miles.
Which Australian nut-producing tree genus, an important bushfood for Aboriginal peoples, was first commercially cultivated at scale not in its native country but in Hawaii?
Macadamia is a genus of four species of trees in the flowering plant family Proteaceae.
This cone-shaped structure at the base of the brainstem controls involuntary functions from heart rate and breathing to vomiting and sneezing — what is it called?
Medulla oblongata is a long stem-like structure which makes up the lower part of the brainstem.
By dividing one cell into two with an identical set of chromosomes apiece, this stage of the cell cycle keeps genetic stability intact across generations — what is it?
Mitosis is a part of the cell cycle in eukaryotic cells in which replicated chromosomes are separated into two new nuclei.

This chronic neurological disorder scrambles the sleep-wake cycle, attacking REM sleep with daytime drowsiness, sleep paralysis, and cataplexy — sudden episodes where muscle tone simply vanishes. What is it?
Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that impairs the ability to regulate sleep-wake cycles, and specifically impacts REM (rapid eye movement) sleep.

Classified using a measurement of weight divided by the square of height, this medical condition is diagnosed when that figure exceeds 30 and is linked to cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes — what is it?
Obesity is a medical condition, considered a disease by multiple organizations, in which excess body fat has accumulated to such an extent that it can have negative effects on health.
Pair it with aspirin and caffeine and it's a first-line remedy for mild headaches; on its own it's the active ingredient many people know as acetaminophen — what is this over-the-counter drug?
Paracetamol is an analgesic and antipyretic agent used to treat fever and mild to moderate pain.
This inflammation of the back of the throat causes a sore throat and fever, most often from a viral infection, though strep bacteria cause roughly a quarter of cases in children — name the condition?
Pharyngitis is inflammation of the back of the throat, known as the pharynx.
Cough, chest pain, fever, and trouble breathing point to this infection of the lungs' alveoli, often classified by where it was caught — community or hospital — what is it?
Pneumonia is an inflammatory condition of the lung primarily affecting the small air sacs known as alveoli.

This sympathomimetic medication is best known as a nasal decongestant, though at higher doses it can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant, making it a common drug of abuse — what's the compound called?
Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic medication which is used as a nasal decongestant to treat nasal congestion.
Named from the Latin word for 'net', this light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye functions much like the film or sensor inside a camera. Name this part of the eye?

This zodiac constellation, whose Latin name means 'archer,' is traditionally depicted as a centaur drawing a bow, and its territory in the southern sky contains the center of the Milky Way galaxy. What constellation is this?
Sagittarius (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere.

Drawing on tools from anthropology, biology, medicine, psychology, and criminology, this scientific field studies human sexual interests, behaviors, and functions, distinct from purely social commentary on the subject — what is this field called?
Sexology is the scientific study of human sexuality, including human sexual interests, behaviors, and functions.
Beginning with stem cells near the basement membrane and passing through two rounds of meiosis, this process turns germ cells into haploid sperm inside the seminiferous tubules — what is it called?
Spermatogenesis is the process by which haploid spermatozoa develop from germ cells in the seminiferous tubules of the testicle.

Practiced by professionals who determine property boundaries and construction points using total stations, GNSS receivers, and lidar sensors, which technical discipline combines geometry, trigonometry, and law?
Surveying is the technique, profession, art, and science of determining the terrestrial positions of points based on the distances and angles between them.

In 1933 he won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries about the role of chromosomes in heredity, studying fruit-fly genetics after the rediscovery of Mendelian inheritance in 1900—who was this pioneering biologist?
Thomas Hunt Morgan (September 25, 1866 - December 4, 1945) was an American evolutionary biologist, geneticist, and embryologist.
Built in the Soviet Union from 1966 to 1989 for short-haul routes, this narrow-body jet earned the NATO codename 'Crusty' — which airliner is it?
Tupolev Tu-134 (NATO reporting name: Crusty) is a twin-engined, narrow-body jet airliner built in the Soviet Union for short and medium-haul routes from 1966 to 1989.

Many of these carrion-eating birds sport a bald head that stays clean while feeding and helps with temperature control — and they'll even urinate on their own legs to cool off. What kind of bird is it?
Vulture is a bird of prey that scavenges on carrion.
Atomic number 30, mined mostly from the ore sphalerite, this metal turns shiny blue-white once its surface oxidation is removed — which element?
Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.
Nicknamed the cell's "molecular unit of currency," this energy-carrying molecule powers muscle contraction and nerve impulses, dropping to ADP or AMP when spent — what is it?
Adenosine triphosphate: Energy-carrying molecule in living cells.
Sometimes called 'emotional blindness,' this condition makes it hard to identify or describe one's own feelings, and affects roughly half of people with autism. What is it?
Alexithymia: Deficiency in understanding, processing, or describing emotions.
Nicknamed the corpse flower for its rotting-flesh stench, this Sumatran plant first bloomed in cultivation at Kew Gardens in 1889 — which species?
Amorphophallus titanum: Species of flowering plant in the arum family Araceae.
NATO code-named 'Condor,' this Soviet-designed four-engine giant is the largest military transport aircraft still flying today — which aircraft?

Antonov An-124 Ruslan: Soviet military transport aircraft. Assembly of the first aircraft begun in 1979; the An-124 (which was sometimes referred to as the An-40 in the West) performed its maiden flight on 24 December 1982.
Most commonly caused by liver cirrhosis and its resulting high blood pressure in the portal system, this condition is the abnormal buildup of fluid in the abdominal cavity — which one?
Ascites: Abnormal build-up of fluid in the abdomen.
Squat-bodied and built for digging, this group includes the European, ferret, honey, and American species despite not truly sharing one family tree — what are they?
According to scholar John Carter, this discipline has two senses: a list of works consulted by an author, and the systematic study of books as physical objects — what's it called?
Bibliography: Organized listing of books and the systematic description of them as objects.

A four-engined American heavy bomber from the 1930s, it dropped more tonnage than any other aircraft in World War II and ranks as the third-most produced bomber in history, after the B-24 and German Ju 88—what is this legendary aircraft?

Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress: American heavy bomber aircraft. The Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress is an American four-engined heavy bomber aircraft that was developed in the mid-1930s for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC).
Also known as undulant fever or Malta fever, this disease is usually caught by drinking unpasteurized milk from infected animals and tends to persist for life — what is it?

Roughly a third of deaths from this group of over 100 diseases trace to tobacco, alcohol, obesity, poor diet and inactivity, and its malignant tumors are defined by uncontrolled cell growth that can spread — what is it?

Cancer: Group of diseases involving cell growth. Cancer is a group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth typically resulting in tumors with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body.

This branch of metabolism breaks down large molecules such as proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids into smaller units, releasing energy as cells convert the leftovers into waste like carbon dioxide and urea — what's it called?
Catabolism: Set of metabolic pathways that breaks down molecules into smaller units.
Sometimes dubbed the 'central science' for sitting between physics and biology, this field studies how matter is composed, behaves, and transforms in reactions — what is it?
Chemistry: Scientific study of matter's behavior and properties.
Named after the French missionary who propagated it in Algeria, this citrus hybrid of mandarin and sweet orange is often sold as an 'Easy-peeler' — which fruit?
Clementine: Hybrid citrus fruit. The exterior is a deep orange colour with a smooth, glossy appearance.
Best known for its powerful, beautiful song, this small Old World flycatcher sometimes hybridizes with a closely related thrush species where their ranges overlap — which bird?
Common nightingale: Species of bird. Its range partly overlaps with that of the more northerly thrush nightingale (Luscinia luscinia), a closely related species with which hybrids have occurred.
Broken down from creatine phosphate in muscle metabolism, this compound is released into the blood at a rate tied to a person's muscle mass — what is it?
Creatinine: Breakdown product of creatine phosphate.
Also called thornapple or devil's trumpet, this genus of nine highly poisonous nightshade plants lent its American name to an outbreak in colonial Jamestown — what genus is it?
Datura: Genus of poisonous, potentially psychoactive plants.

This colourless, water-mixable lab solvent is technically odorless — but degraded samples reek of fish thanks to a dimethylamine impurity. It's better known by a three-letter abbreviation; what's the compound?
Dimethylformamide: Chemical compound. Dimethylformamide, DMF is an organic compound with the chemical formula HCON(CH3)2.
This German-born British economist championed 'human-scale, appropriate technology' in his 1973 book, later ranked among the 100 most influential books since World War II — who was he?
E. F. Schumacher: British statistician and economist (1911–1977)
This messenger network of hormone feedback loops releases chemicals from internal glands like the thyroid, pituitary, and adrenal glands straight into the bloodstream to regulate distant organs?
Endocrine system: Hormone-producing glands of a body.

A women's-rights campaigner schooled in 1830s New York, she was the first scientist to show certain gases trap heat — anticipating that rising CO2 could warm the climate. Who was this overlooked pioneer?
Eunice Newton Foote: American scientist and activist (1819–1888)
This genus of small-to-medium wildcats — ranging from the diminutive black-footed cat to the larger jungle cat — also includes humanity's domestic pet, the housecat — which genus?
Home to the radius and ulna joined by the interosseous membrane, this region of the arm lies between the elbow and the wrist — what is it?
Forearm: Region of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist.
Often triggered by H. pylori infection or NSAID use, this inflammation of the stomach lining can, in its autoimmune form, lead to pernicious anemia — what condition is it?
Gastritis: Inflammation of the stomach lining. It may occur as a short episode or have a long duration.
Produced by the pancreas's alpha cells, this hormone raises blood sugar by triggering the liver to break down stored glycogen — the functional opposite of insulin. What is it?
Glucagon: Peptide hormone. It raises the concentration of glucose and fatty acids in the bloodstream and is considered to be the main catabolic hormone of the body.
This motorsport engineer led the Haas Formula One team from 2016 to 2023 before becoming CEO of a MotoGP outfit — who is he?
Guenther Steiner: Italian and American motor racing engineer (born 1965)
Also known as the Burgundy snail and served as escargot, this large air-breathing land snail native to Europe has a globular brown shell — what species is it?
Discovered in 2013 in South Africa's Rising Star Cave system, this small-brained archaic human species yielded over 1,500 bone specimens from at least 15 individuals — which species?
Homo naledi: South African archaic human species. The initial discovery comprises 1,550 specimens of bone, representing 737 different skeletal elements, and at least 15 different individuals.

Diagnosed via Whipple's triad and most often triggered by diabetes medications like insulin, this condition causes shakiness, confusion, and sweating when blood sugar drops below 70 mg/dL — what is it?

Hypoglycemia: Decrease in blood sugar. It is defined as blood glucose below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), symptoms associated with hypoglycemia, and resolution of symptoms when blood sugar returns to normal.
This cerebrovascular condition is a localized ballooning of a brain blood vessel most often found in the Circle of Willis, with the 'berry'-shaped type being the most common. What is it?

Intracranial aneurysm: Ballooning or rupturing of a blood vessel in the brain. The risk of rupture varies with the size and location of the aneurysm, with those in the posterior circulation being more prone to rupture.
Enlisting disguised as a man named 'Jean' on Bougainville's expedition, this expert botanist became the first woman to circumnavigate the globe — who is she?
Jeanne Baret: French explorer, naturalist, botanist (1740–1807)
Personal physician to the Buddha and King Bimbisāra in 5th-century BCE Rājagṛha, this 'Medicine King' is still revered by traditional healers across Asia — who is he?

Jīvaka: Personal physician of the Buddha and Indian King Bimbisara. Jīvaka (Pali: Jīvaka Komārabhacca; Sanskrit: Jīvaka Kaumārabhṛtya) was the personal physician (Sanskrit: vaidya) of the Buddha and the Indian King Bimbisāra.
Named from Greek words for 'hare' and 'form,' this mammalian order splits into rabbits-and-hares on one branch and pikas on the other, totaling around 110 living species — which order?
Formed by cross-linking phenolic precursors, this class of complex organic polymers gives rigidity to plant cell walls, especially in wood and bark — what is it?
Lignin: Structural phenolic polymer in plant cell walls.
Native to Afghanistan and Iran, this herb tastes like an intensified cross between celery and parsley, with seeds used much like fennel — what is it?
Nicknamed the 'tree of death' and 'beach apple,' this small-fruited tropical tree oozes a milky sap so toxic it can blister skin on contact — which tree?
Manchineel: Poisonous plant from tropical North and South America.

Spanning everything from sacred religious writings to the exuberantly profane, and often grouped by place, language, and genre, what broad body of European writing falls between late antiquity and the Renaissance?
Medieval literature: Literary works of the Middle Ages.
This scientific field studies microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi, and protists, encompassing sub-disciplines like virology and mycology — which discipline?
Ranging from a tiny 8-inch species to the 10-foot Komodo dragon, this reptile genus includes an extinct relative that may have grown over 20 feet long — what are they called?
Monitor lizard: Genus of reptiles. Monitor lizards are lizards in the genus Varanus, the only extant genus in the family Varanidae.
Named for its resemblance to a tiny mouse's ear, this flowering plant genus is known in the Northern Hemisphere by a romantic common name and is Alaska's official flower — what is it?
Myosotis: Genus of flowering plants in the family Boraginaceae.
Also known as black cumin or kalonji, this flowering plant native to the Levant and Iran is used across the world as a culinary spice — which species is it?
Nigella sativa: Species of flowering plant in the buttercup family.
Sold under the brand name Zyprexa, this atypical antipsychotic treats schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and is sometimes used off-label to fight chemotherapy-induced nausea — what is this drug?
Olanzapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Olanzapine, sold under the brand name Zyprexa among others, is an atypical antipsychotic primarily used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
A pale-blue gas with a chlorine-like pungent odour, this unstable three-atom cousin of oxygen forms by UV light and electrical discharges and shields us high in the stratosphere — what is it?
This thick, fan-shaped muscle underlies the breast and is responsible for flexing, adducting, and internally rotating the upper arm — which chest muscle?
Pectoralis major: Main human chest muscle.

Nicknamed 'terror birds,' this family of large, mostly flightless carnivores roamed the Americas from the Cenozoic era, with one genus, Titanis, reaching as far as the southern United States — which family?
Phorusrhacidae: Extinct family of flightless birds. The exact number of genera is uncertain, as some taxa such as Brontornis may be different forms of bird instead.

Proposed in 1904 and finally proven a century later using Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow techniques, this problem asks whether any loop-shrinkable finite 3D space must be a hypersphere — which famous problem?
Poincaré conjecture: Theorem in geometric topology.
Nearly odorless with a faintly sweet taste, this diol is approved as a food additive under E-number E1520 and serves as a solvent vehicle in many medications — which compound?
Propylene glycol: Chemical compound. Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
Also known as the holly oak, this large evergreen tree native to the Mediterranean produces acorns that mature within a single summer — which species is it?
Quercus ilex: Oak tree species native to the Mediterranean.

Almost exclusively affecting girls and emerging by 18 months of age, this genetic disorder — usually caused by a mutation in the MECP2 gene — brings language and coordination loss along with repetitive hand movements. What is it?
Rett syndrome: Genetic brain disorder. Rett syndrome (RTT) is a genetic disorder that typically becomes apparent after 6–18 months of age and almost exclusively in girls.

Also called 'German measles,' this vaccine-preventable viral infection is usually mild but can cause severe birth defects — including cataracts and deafness — if a mother catches it early in pregnancy. What disease is it?
Rubella: Human viral disease. Rubella, also known as German measles or three-day measles, is a vaccine-preventable infection caused by the rubella virus.
Named after the Latin word for a small shovel, this flat triangular bone connects the upper arm bone to the collarbone and forms the back of the shoulder girdle — what is it?
Scapula: Bone that connects the humerus and clavicle.
An adult female of this ruminant is a ewe, a castrated male a wether, and a young one a lamb — and with about 1.2 billion of them, they're easily the most common of their kind. What animal?
Sheep: Domesticated ruminant bred for meat, wool, and milk.
Nicknamed a 'truth serum' in popular culture despite dubious real-world reliability, this fast-acting barbiturate anesthetic is marketed under the brand name Pentothal — which drug?
Sodium thiopental: Barbiturate general anesthetic. It is the thiobarbiturate analog of pentobarbital, and an analog of thiobarbital.
This Polish-American DuPont chemist invented a super-strong polymer fiber and became the fourth woman ever inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame — who was she?
Stephanie Kwolek: American chemist who invented Kevlar (1923–2014)
Defined by a single skull opening behind each eye socket that anchors larger jaw muscles, this major branch of the amniote family tree includes all mammals and their extinct kin — which clade?
Synapsida: Clade of tetrapods. Synapsida is a diverse group of tetrapod vertebrates that includes all mammals and their extinct relatives.
Patented in 1953 and originally derived from Streptomyces bacteria, this antibiotic treats ailments from acne to cholera to plague by blocking bacterial protein production — which drug?
Tetracycline: Antibiotic. It is available in oral and topical formulations.
Home to more than 4,200 described species, this family of large crane flies can be identified by the length of their maxillary palps — what is it?
Tipulidae: Family of flies. There are more than 30 genera and 4,200 described species in Tipulidae, common and widespread throughout the world.
Element 74 boasts the highest melting point of any known element — a scorching 3,422 °C — and carries the symbol W from its German name. Which metal is it?
Tungsten: Chemical element with atomic number 74 (W)
Released from the posterior pituitary when body fluids get too concentrated, this hormone helps kidneys reabsorb water and may also influence pair bonding — what is it?
Vasopressin: Mammalian hormone released from the pituitary gland.
Nicknamed the 'cock-of-the-woods,' this ground-dwelling grouse is the largest of all its kind, with males growing to nearly twice the size of females — which bird?
Western capercaillie: Species of bird. The bird shows extreme sexual dimorphism, with males nearly twice the size of females.
Nicknamed the ZZ plant or eternity plant, this glossy-leaved houseplant genus native to eastern Africa is prized for being nearly impossible to kill — name the genus?
Zamioculcas: Species of plant. Zamioculcas is a genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae, containing the single species Zamioculcas zamiifolia.
Xenon is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for xenon is Xe. Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
Bismuth is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for bismuth is Bi. Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.

Bette Midler is a comedian. Bette Midler ( bet MID-lər; born December 1, 1945) is an American actress, comedian, singer, and author.
In what year was Bill Paxton born?
Bill Paxton: William Paxton (May 17, 1955 – February 25, 2017) was an American actor, filmmaker and musician.
In what year was Suki Waterhouse born?
Suki Waterhouse: Alice Suki Waterhouse (born 5 January 1992) is an English actress, singer, and model.
